I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $2166 and four fully developed properties. The opponent has $94 but owns heavily mortgaged holdings with only a few active properties.

The bank has no houses left. Hotels cannot be broken down without replacement houses. This constraint is central to my strategy.

I am weighing whether to build hotels on the pink properties. This costs $300 but returns 12 houses to the bank. The opponent's only liquid assets are $94 and eight red houses, worth $600. Their Virginia rent of $700 would bankrupt them. Building hotels would let them break down their own hotels and sell houses to survive.

I decided against building hotels on the pinks. Unmortgaging the railroad or Tennessee would be too expensive and offers little rent. I am now considering whether to trade.

Trading cash would help the opponent survive. Completing their orange monopoly is dangerous because they could build there if they sell red houses to acquire replacement houses.

I will end my turn. I have no trade to offer and no building or selling to do.
